text: Compressing a file shrinks it by removing redundancy, so it takes less storage and transfers faster; anyone can decompress it. Encrypting a file scrambles its contents so only someone with the correct key can read it, protecting privacy without necessarily changing size. For example, people zip photos before emailing them, while online banking encrypts your login details.
task: Explain the difference between compressing a file and encrypting it, including one everyday use of each.
